38.name: ATTACK
38.why: Two producers 0x005148B3/0x00514B37 in GmCoreAction.cpp, both containing GmCoreAction.cpp:933 'action < WORLD_ACTIONS' and :934 'AvValidate(targetAgentId)' -- so field 1 is the client's targetAgentId. The six-arm jump table at 0x00514984 sends 0x0026 / 0x0033 / 0x0039 / 0x003F from arms 0-3: four c2s opcodes, ONE switch, ONE targetAgentId, so attack and interact cannot be the same intent. Arm 0 alone is gated on MsCliApiGetMap()==MISSION_MAP_GAME (call 0x0084D9B0 @0x0081668C), fed by the third dword of GAME_SMSG 0x0199. 64.name: ROTATE_PLAYER
64.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary. Field 1 is an ANGLE IN RADIANS and field 2 is a normalised turn amount in (0,1]. Both are marshalled as u32 -- which is what the client's own SEND table says ([u32,u32], wire 10 bytes), so the typing here is CORRECT and must not be 'fixed' to float -- while their VALUES are IEEE-754 float32. THREE INDEPENDENT LEGS. (1) The client names the quantity itself: the public entry 0x008165C0 range-checks its float argument against the assert text `(rotation >= -1.0f) && (rotation <= 1.0f)` from P:\Code\Gw\Char\Cli\ChCliApi.cpp line 5562, then tail-calls the sender; that argument becomes field 2 (as its absolute value) and decides field 1's sign. There is exactly ONE site in the image that sends 0x0040 -- the 12-byte wrapper at 0x009207B0, found by enumerating all 174 callers of the channel send 0x007DCF00 and recovering the opcode immediate at each. (2) The +/-inf in field 1 is a literal SENTINEL, not a computed ratio: the sender loads +inf from .rdata 0x00948654 when rotation > 0 and -inf from 0x0094E538 when rotation < 0, and when rotation is exactly 0 sends atan2(current facing) with field 2 = 1.0. So an infinity means 'turning continuously, sign gives the direction' -- it does NOT rule out an angle, which is the inference that kept this opcode unnamed. (3) The wire agrees: of 559 samples across 55 game-channel streams, field 1 is never NaN and every one of the 163 finite values lies inside +/-pi (max 3.0190), and 16 of 162 equal atan2(dir.y,dir.x) of a nearby 0x003D direction vector to float32 round-off, 33 within 0.05 rad, against a null model whose 95th percentile is 5. WHICH SIGN IS A LEFT TURN IS UNVERIFIED (121/189 and 106/169 -- real but weak); no left/right claim is made here. CORRECTION TO THIS ENTRY'S OWN EARLIER TEXT: 'field 2 is exactly 1.0 in all 12 observed samples' was true of those twelve and false as a generalisation -- it is 1.0 in 433 of 559, with 105 at 0.425 and a tail down to 0.10133, which CORROBORATES studies/divergence/FINDINGS.md R3 (411/536 and 105 before the 2026-08-10 runs existed) rather than refuting it. The floor is the client's own send gate: it refuses to send below 0.1, and the observed minimum is 0.10133. CORPUS CAVEAT: 536 of the 559 are the harness clicking fixed window fractions, 22 are 2026-08-10 loopback (17 of them tape-loaded), and 1 is live -- so the FREQUENCIES describe our own driver, not a player. The name does not rest on them; it rests on the binary. UPSTREAM ldufr/Headquarter numbers ROTATE_PLAYER 0x0040 independently (GWCA has 0x003E, the known +2 drift); see PLAN.md 6.1 for its register row. Evidence: vault/captures/live/20260807T143055 conn :60935 msg 52 (field1 = 1.08214450 rad = 62.0026 deg, exactly atan2 of the (360.53,678.12) direction the three preceding 0x003D carry), and toolkit/authsrv/test_rotate.py, which re-measures the wire-side invariants every run.

10.name: SEND_MACHINE_SPEC
10.why: Builder 0x00491820 has ZERO call sites: it is registered as a connection-established CALLBACK ('push 0x491820' at 0x00491BD9 into the connection factory), guarded to run at most once per process by a four-dword zero test. Every field traces to a Windows API: ole32!CoCreateGuid (resolved by name) for the blob, KERNEL32!GetSystemInfo dwNumberOfProcessors, CPUID leaves 0 and 1 (vendor string; 'and ecx,0xfff' signature), ntdll!RtlGetVersion major/minor/build, GlobalMemoryStatusEx >>20 for MB, and a literal 0x9020 stored when d3d9.dll loads. The frame arithmetic closes to the byte: base -0x238, last field ends at base+0xF0 = 240, matching 'push 0xf0'. Wire checks that could have failed: field 9 == 36896 == 0x9020 exactly; field 5 decodes to a valid 12-byte CPUID vendor string in both sessions; the blob is a structurally valid RFC4122 v4 UUID in both draws and DIFFERS between sessions on the same machine, which kills the machine-fingerprint reading. Fire-and-forget: the client sends its next message in the same TCP flush without waiting. Fields 10/11 (adapter PCI vendor/device) are INFERRED, field 12 UNVERIFIED. Prior art: authsrv.py:111-114 already reads 0x000A/0x000B as the computer-info pair -- that is OUR reconstruction and corroborates nothing; what is new is the per-field API trace.

18.name: REQUEST_QUEST_INFO
18.why: Thunk 0x0091FC00, one caller 0x0080DE09 inside 0x0080DDD0, whose assert ChCliApi.cpp:4253 'context->challengeSortArray.Find(challenge)' sits 18 bytes before the send call IN THE SAME FUNCTION -- the client's word for the argument is 'challenge'. It is a FETCH, not a push: both callers (QuestTaskTracker, QuestChallenge) reach the sender only on the FAILURE branch of a description lookup (0x0080DBE0 = 'test byte [esi+4],1; jne; xor eax,eax; ret'), and the alternative branch is assert(false) at QuestTaskTracker.cpp:299. Reply seals it: GAME_SMSG 0x004C on the same connection in 30.7-61.5 ms with field 1 equal to the requested id, 16 of 16, carrying two encoded strings. Cross-check the corpus could have failed: every 0x003B with code 0x01 is followed by exactly one 0x0012 carrying that id and no other code ever is -- 5 for 5 in each session, both directions. Consider REQUEST_QUEST_DESCRIPTION as the narrower alternative; the reply is a description.

59.name: NPC_SERVICE_SELECT
59.why: Builder 0x00920670 ({0x3B, arg}), sole entry 0x00816340 with 8 callers across GmNpc.cpp, VnLearnSkill.cpp, VnUnlockSkill.cpp, VnUnlockItem.cpp, VnUnlockHero.cpp -- a bank of NPC service windows, not just quests. The argument is a tagged selection id: five call sites OR in distinct high tags (0x0A000000, 0x0E000000, 0x0F000000, 0x10000000, 0x1000<<16) and VnUnlockItem masks with 0xFFFFFF first, which proves the low 24 bits are the parameter. OBSERVED: all 22 wire samples are the 0x00800000 family decoding as 0x800000|(quest_id<<8)|code, and 11 of 11 firings in the narrated session match a narrated NPC action in order, with phase alignment checked at all three map-transfer boundaries. The single code-0x04 in the whole corpus lands strictly between the two Abbey transfers, on the only narrated mid-quest step. Named SELECT rather than DIALOG because 'dialog' is our word and five of the eight call sites are service windows. 62.name: MOVE_TO_COORD
62.why: Thunk 0x00920720 <- entry 0x008164C0 <- the tail of the walk-module function 0x00535490, which caches a commanded destination in statics 0xC07C2C/30/34 and sends only when it CHANGES. Its counterpart 0x00535570 writes +inf (0x00948654) into those statics and calls the 0x0047 sender instead: cancel the destination, then report position. The asymmetry that settles it: 0x008164C0 passes its own ARGUMENT pointer to the sender, while the 0x0047 entry 0x008167F0 fills its buffer from playerControlledChar via 0x005FC400 -- so this vec2 cannot be the player's position. On the wire the server agrees: 6 of 15 draw an AGENT_MOVE_TO_POINT for the player's own agent 33-65 ms later whose destination is bit-identical to the sent vec2. 43.why: OBSERVED for the mechanism, MEDIUM for the NAME, and the split is the point. Build 38797. THE MECHANISM: wrapper 0x00920230 writes the opcode as an immediate (0x0092024B `mov dword [ebp-0x50], 0x2b`) and asserts CharMsg.cpp:8129 `knotCount <= arrsize(message.knotData)` @0x00920262. SOLE PRODUCER IMAGE-WIDE, established twice by methods that share no premise. (1) The wrapper has exactly ONE direct reference, thunk 0x00816110, which has exactly ONE caller, 0x008C08DC, and neither VA occurs as a stored dword at any alignment in ANY of the five sections -- so neither is in a vtable, and not even a runtime-built table could hold one, since the store's immediate would itself be in .text. (2) A value-first sweep that cannot desync: of 134 materialisations of 0x2b in .text across six encodings, exactly ONE instruction sits inside the body of a function that calls a send entry -- 0x0092024B -- swept over all 214 send call sites, which is the CORRECTED census (there are TWO send entries, 0x007DCF00 and the dword-array variant 0x007DCB10 with 40 sites of its own; the earlier 174 missed the second). Controls on 0x78/0x39/0x3d/0x2c/0x40 each find their producer, and 0x40 surfaces six candidates that separate on which slot the buffer's `lea` names, so the method CAN report a second one. Reachability of the call site was tested rather than assumed: reverse closure over 135,455 direct call edges from the enclosing function 0x008C0840 converges at depth 25 on NINE functions, all inside 0x008BA79D..0x008C0840, no Gm* module anywhere. FIELD 1 IS A CLIENT-ALLOCATED STROKE HANDLE, not a target and not an agent: it is [canvas+0xbc], written at 0x008C0065 either by popping the back of a recycle pool at [canvas+0x68] or from the post-increment counter at [canvas+0x98], and the client looks its OWN line up with the key {0, that handle} at 0x008BF427-0x008BF442. Two wire facts corroborate the allocator and rule out a colour or ping-type reading: our corpus emits 7 then 6 (a DECREASING pair no plain counter produces), and two flushes 250 ms apart that are one stroke SHARE id 6 while two separate strokes 250 ms apart differ. A server must ECHO it in GAME_SMSG 0x0091 field 2, never invent it. FIELD 2 IS A POLYLINE IN TERRAIN CELLS. Each u32 packs two SIGNED int16, LOW HALF = x: the pack is 0x00920280-0x00920291, and the encoder at 0x008C07F0 divides each world float by the double 96.0 at 0x0094DE10 -- the terrain cell pitch -- AFTER 0x008C0560 has added the player's own world position, so the value is ABSOLUTE world/96 and not an offset. The receive side multiplies by that same constant at three sites (0x008BF177, 0x008BE6C7, 0x008BE774) and sign-extends both halves with movsx at 0x0091EA60/0x0091EA67. THE WIRE DISCRIMINATES ALL OF THAT and could have refuted it: the client's own constants bound a compass click at sqrt(0.1650390625) * 11076.9228515625 = 4500.0 world units exactly (hit test 0x008C0130 vs the world scale 0x00BA0318), and the corpus's one live sample -- 20260807T143055 conn :60935 t=50.702, `[32811, 7, [3801175]]`, knot 0x003A0057 -- lands at (8352, 5568), 3236.4 units from the position the preceding 0x003D reports 150 ms earlier and 5.0 degrees off that message's own heading, while the three rivals (halves swapped 7140.1, unscaled 11562.4, unscaled+swapped 11580.7) are all OUTSIDE the compass. Eight further knots in vault/captures/authsrv/authsrv-20260805T214038-c2.jsonl carry a NEGATIVE low half, which under an unsigned read would sit 6.29e6 units away. RATE: knots accumulate at a 25 ms floor (0x008BF45E `cmp ecx,0x19`, and a faster sample UPDATES the last knot in place) and flush on a 250 MILLISECOND countdown (0x008C08B8 `mov eax,0xfa`), sending nothing when empty -- so a drag is at most 10 knots per message and the 16 cap is never approached. The unit is milliseconds on three witnesses: the clock is WINMM!timeGetTime (import at 0x009396F8 via 0x0046B4E0 -> 0x0047F730), the same delta is divided by the literal 1000.0 at 0x008C0877, and OUR OWN CAPTURES show consecutive flushes of one stroke at 0.251988 s and 0.249950 s. A single knot is a click (a ping), a run is a drag. WHY THE NAME IS ONLY MEDIUM: the SEND side names nothing but `knotCount` and `message.knotData`. 145.name: COMPASS_DRAW_BROADCAST
145.why: OBSERVED, from build 38797's own binary; ZERO live samples exist and the name rests entirely on the chain, which is why the chain is given whole. HIGH here where GAME_CMSG 43 is only MEDIUM, because THIS end names itself: handler 0x0091EA20 asserts CharMsg.cpp:4934 `message.knotCount <= CHAR_MAX_DRAW_MINIMAP_KNOT_COUNT` @0x0091EA43 -- the ONLY occurrence of the substring MINIMAP anywhere in the image (1 ASCII hit at 0xbc8c9f, inside that expression; 0 UTF-16). It posts frame message 0x1000009E via 0x00812140; a sweep of every `push <frame msgId>` in .text classified by the call that follows shows 0x1000009E with EXACTLY ONE POSTER AND EXACTLY ONE SUBSCRIBER -- Compass.cpp at 0x008BB5D7 -- against controls that are not degenerate (0x10000090 has 1 poster and 3 subscribers; 0x1000014E has 2 and 7). Compass.cpp's frame proc dispatches it at 0x008BBF38 into CompassCanvas's 0x008BE680, which appends the knots to a polyline; and the polyline renderer -- the function holding `CompassCanvas.cpp:1372 knotCount >= 2` @0x008c11b2 -- is 0x008C10D8, whose ONLY caller is 0x008C0840, the same function that flushes knots to the server. One function draws the ink and sends it. (The last hop, subscription handle -> which switch arm -> the point array, is NOT disassembled: the subscribe passes a control handle rather than a callback, so that step is RECONSTRUCTION.) IT IS GAME_CMSG 0x002B PLUS A LEADING u16, AND THE u16 IS AN OWNER TAG WHOSE LOCAL VALUE IS ZERO. Fields 1 and 2 are used for exactly one thing: as the two components of the key passed to the line lookup at 0x008BE696-0x008BE6A1, and the client builds that same key for its OWN strokes with the first component hard-zeroed -- 0x008C0091 `mov dword [esi],0` on creation and 0x008BF43B `mov dword [ebp-8],0` on the drag-path lookup. SO A REBROADCAST MUST CARRY A NON-ZERO FIELD 1 or the drawing client merges the echo into its own line and doubles the stroke. Nothing in the compass group resolves field 1 to an agent, a name or a colour, and the client types it u16 (cmd 0x204) rather than with its type-0 agent_id tag, so 'sender id' is RECONSTRUCTION about the number space and OBSERVED only as identity; what number space it draws from is NOT FOUND. Field 2 is the client's own stroke handle coming back (GAME_CMSG 0x002B field 1). Field 3 is the polyline: two SIGNED int16 per u32 with the LOW HALF FIRST, sign-extended by the movsx at 0x0091EA60/0x0091EA67 and multiplied back by the double 96.0 at 0x0094DE10 in all three consumers -- the exact inverse of the sender's divide at 0x008C07FB -- so knots are ABSOLUTE world coordinates in terrain cells and must be near the player to be inside the compass at all. A knotCount of 1 on a key with no existing line draws a PING RIPPLE instead of a line (0x008BE6B3 `cmp edi,1`) in the colour whose static initialiser at 0x00BFAC24 is 0xFFFF0000, opaque red -- which is what GWW documents a compass ping to be, and is the cheapest possible server-side demonstration. THE OVER-RANGE HAZARD IS VOID AND THIS ENTRY EXISTS PARTLY TO RETIRE IT: studies/minimap/FINDINGS.md 4.1 warned that a knotCount > 16 walks past knotData[16] into the security cookie and fast-fails the PROCESS. Every clause about the HANDLER is true (it re-loads the count at 0x0091EA52 AFTER the assert returns, the destination array is [ebp-0x84,ebp-0x04) with `sub esp,0x84` = 128+4, and 0x0091EA9E calls __security_check_cookie before the epilogue) -- but MsgConn.cpp's generic unpacker refuses the message first: 0x007DC455 `shr eax,8` reads the declared capacity out of the cmd (0x102b -> 16), 0x007DC458 `cmp ecx,eax`, 0x007DC45A `ja 0x007DC620`, which sets error state 2 and returns WITHOUT storing the count and WITHOUT ever calling the dispatch member at 0x007DC5C4. The bound is tight, no off-by-one, so CharMsg:4934 is unreachable from the network and an over-range send is INERT rather than dangerous -- it measures nothing. NAMING HAZARD: GAME_CMSG 0x0091 is a DIFFERENT, already-handled message -- `[u8, u8]`, 4 bytes, SEND table 0x00BCB030, bound in toolkit/authsrv/authsrv.py:980 as GAME_CMSG_INSTANCE_LOAD_REQUEST_ITEMS with a live dispatch arm. Different channel dict, one line away from a reader conflating them. Live count 0 of 22,524 s2c GAME_SMSG, which is expected rather than absent evidence: draws are party-visible and every live capture is a solo operator. Our server sends nothing on this opcode and drops its c2s partner.
